html:
The Rössing uranium mine in the Namib desert near Swakopmund began production in 1976 and is one of the largest open pit uranium mines in the world.

It was opened under South African rule by the British firm Rio Tinto, and its sales during the occupation broke United Nations rules on Namibia's resources. After independence it became one of the main exporters and employers.

Uranium has made Namibia one of the world's leading producers, along with the diamonds of the coast. In 2019 Rio Tinto sold its share to a Chinese state company, part of China's growing role in African mining, fuelling nuclear power abroad.
sum: The Rössing uranium mine in the Namib desert near Swakopmund began production in 1976 and is one of the largest open pit uranium mines in the world.
